notes: Egress proxy blocks Poly Haven / ambientCG / all CDNs: every asset is procedural.
Screenshot tool renders through SwiftShader (software GL); fps in shots/*.json is NOT a GPU number. Draw calls, triangles and errors are real.

Wave 1 was interrupted mid-round by an API spend limit. Builders were killed before writing module READMEs and before their final iteration passes. Scores below are the ORCHESTRATOR's own integration review, not a full critic pass: fewer angles, no API-contract audit. Treat them as provisional and biased slightly optimistic on modules only seen at one preset.
Integration verified: all 8 wave-1 modules load together in the full game with zero console errors, 50 draw calls, 1.22 M triangles.

SECOND ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: environment/index.js clamped auto-exposure at 60x, and it was hitting 5.46x at golden hour / 60x at night on ordinary, correctly-lit scenes (Math.max(0, keyDir.y) kills the key-light term well before the sky actually looks dim as the sun nears the horizon). Every material several-fold overexposed, verified by reading a baked lion albedo texture directly (correct ~0.38 linear) against near-white on screen. Lowered the ceiling to 4 (commit e3a6999); night is now dim and legible with visible stars instead of blown to white, golden hour shows correct value separation between light/dark test objects instead of clipping everything. Needs a further tuning pass against real references but is no longer broken. This, independently of the sRGB double-encode, explains why several modules' screenshots looked washed out at low sun angles even after the sRGB fix — e.g. buildings' lodge preset (tod 17.5) flat-white background buildings.

THIRD ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: terrain/mesh.js had `mesh.receiveShadow = false; // BENCH`, a leftover benchmarking flag that silently blocked every shadow in the game from landing on the ground, anywhere. Fixed (commit e3a6999). This was the real cause of animals' round-1 'no contact shadow' blocker — animals had already shipped a drawn contact-shadow decal as a workaround, which stays in place as a complement now that real shadows also work.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-02: core/Textures.js gpu() double-encoded sRGB (shader-side linearToSRGBv plus an sRGB-internal-format render target). Linear 0.216 was stored as byte 188 instead of 128 — every albedo ~37% too bright. This, not ACES tone mapping, was the real cause of the project-wide washed-out look; the earlier 'author darker to compensate' guidance was a workaround over a core defect and is now WRONG. Core is fixed. Modules that compensated must have that compensation REMOVED: props is currently over-dark (near-black foliage), and any darkening added to animals/terrain/roads in round 2 must be re-checked.

issues.text: FIXED (integrator, commit e3a6999) and verified: the exposure ceiling was 60, hitting 5.46x at golden hour and 60x at night — every material several-fold overexposed. Lowered to 4 for day/golden-hour. Verified: golden-hour test spheres now show correct value separation (dark box reads dark, gold sphere reads gold) instead of clipping to white.

FIXED (integrator, follow-up) and verified against animals' own ground-level night screenshot: the single ceiling of 4 fixed golden hour but left true night essentially unlit black (no HemisphereLight exists in this architecture; ambient is entirely IBL-via-exposure). Gated a separate, higher night-only ceiling (12) on `isMoonKey`. Verified: night is now dim but clearly readable — grass, animal silhouettes, a waterhole with reflection, river and escarpment all visible, not blown white or crushed black.
Hard dark band at the horizon where the sky dome meets its ground colour — not yet independently re-checked since the exposure fixes; may look different now.

Golden-hour sky washes toward white at the horizon with no blue retained overhead — a separate, still-open atmosphere-authoring issue distinct from the exposure clamp (confirmed distinct: the exposure fix changed object brightness but not this sky-colour behaviour).

environment.good: Scattering gradient at noon is correct and clean; golden-hour light direction and long soft shadows are convincing; CSM works; zero errors. Both exposure regimes (day and night) are now correctly calibrated after two rounds of fixes — this was the single highest-leverage module in the project, since its exposure bug was silently degrading the visual score of terrain, props, animals and buildings at low sun angles.

issues.text: FIXED and verified: real cast shadows confirmed working (terrain's receiveShadow flag was the root cause, fixed by the integrator); the module's own contact-shadow decal was correctly demoted from primary grounding cue to a small low-opacity AO term to avoid double-darkening now both exist.

FIXED and verified: a real bug where the staged waterhole's ground height sampled at the pool's outer rim could grab an unrelated rise and float the whole water plane over a metre above drinking animals — fixed by averaging samples inside the footprint instead (tools/shots/animals-waterhole-r6.png).

FIXED (jointly with environment) and verified: night was essentially unlit black after the first exposure-ceiling fix; animals' own precise ground-level evidence (tools/shots/animals-night-r4.png) is what led to the isMoonKey-gated night ceiling fix. Re-verified after: night now reads as dim, legible moonlit savannah (tools/shots/animals-night-ceilingfix.png).
Elephant skin bump pattern reads slightly too regular/geometric ('golf ball') rather than organic wrinkles.

Wrinkle normal scale and leg anatomy were addressed by the builder in round 2 (taper, knee/hock joints, reduced normal strength) but not independently re-verified with a fresh close-up by the orchestrator.

animals.good: The procedural elephant is unmistakably an elephant — trunk taper, tusks, ear shape and back line all read correctly from code-built geometry, still the hardest thing in the project. Real cast shadows, correct grey hide tone, and a fixed waterhole all independently verified across three rounds. The builder's own precise diagnostic work (reading back a baked texture to prove an exposure bug rather than a colour bug) is what led directly to two of the project's highest-leverage core fixes.

Delivers habitat quality per species, animal happiness driving births/deaths/migration, visitor arrivals driven by reputation and price, a full income/expense ledger (tickets, lodge, shop vs staff, buildings, roads, feed, vet, interest), staff morale feeding upkeep efficiency, village prosperity, seeded events (drought, disease, poachers, viral review, grant) and poaching risk tied to ranger staffing. 58/58 tests pass, determinism verified.

issues.text: The showcase scene is blown out to near-white, so the passes cannot be judged. Cause is almost certainly that `environment` is not loaded in the effects showcase, so nobody sets renderer.toneMappingExposure and it stays at 1.0 under a bright sun. Add environment to the showcase's optional deps or set a sane exposure in stage().

204 draw calls at overview is far above the '≤12 extra draw calls' budget. Most are probably the showcase's own test geometry rather than the pipeline, but the module must measure and report the pipeline's own cost separately.
No A/B of the `off` preset against `overview` has been done, so the pipeline's actual contribution is unmeasured.

issues.text: FIXED and verified (tools/shots/buildings-final-lodge.png): the flat-black roof shadow is gone — this was the environment exposure clamp + terrain receiveShadow bugs, both since fixed, not a buildings issue. The ground in front of the lodge now reads as correctly lit dry grass with a real soft shadow, and the background buildings show proper thatch roofs and shaded plaster walls instead of flat white boxes. Closes the loop on a cross-cutting bug chain: animals found it, environment/terrain fixed it, buildings independently confirms the fix.

Root cause found and fixed by the builder: the showcase's 8 hand-picked site anchors landed on/near water/kopjes for every candidate on this seed (0/240 valid), so the whole complex fell back to a coordinate that was itself underwater — the actual cause of earlier 'floating on water' renders. Replaced with a full-grid scan with biome/water-table rejection and slope scoring.

Buildings-only cost measured directly via api.stats(): 34 draw calls / 131,730 triangles for 25 buildings across all 16 catalogue types — well inside the <=60/<=400k spec budget. The ~276-296 draw calls seen in full-frame screenshots is terrain+props, not buildings; earlier concern about the draw-call count was based on the wrong number.

Builder's own README, honest: occasional forced placement when local slope fails even on a good site (2/25 this seed, never on water); no LOD beyond 300m; several catalogue types (fence gate, feeder, toilets, parking) only shown at overview distance, not close-up.

Two real bugs found and fixed along the way (site placement, windpump rotor pivot). All 6 presets load, zero errors, lint clean, buildings' own draw-call cost is well within budget.

Vegetation existing at all was the single biggest blocker in the project three rounds ago; it is now a strong module.

issues.text: Verification took several attempts because the overview preset (camera distance 430m) makes a 4-5m vehicle imperceptibly small — I initially misread this as 'no vehicles rendering' and, worse, briefly misdiagnosed it as a missing kit.setBodyMatrix() call based on a flawed grep pattern ('setMatrix' is not a substring of 'setBodyMatrix') before re-checking and finding the wiring is correct. The close preset settles it cleanly: vehicles are real, positioned, and rendering. Recorded so the mistake isn't repeated.

Overview preset's vehicle scale-at-distance is a legitimate framing concern for the module's own showcase, even though it isn't a rendering bug — worth a closer default camera or a labelled close-up inset.

traffic.good: Genuinely good: a real open safari truck with tiered bench seats, clearly visible seated passengers in varied clothing colours, ribbed canopy roof, roof rack, spare wheel, khaki body paint, and a visible ground contact shadow. World-state vehicle spawning verified directly (6 vehicles with plausible, in-bounds positions). Zero console errors, 106 draw calls at close, all modules load together cleanly.

issues.text: terrain/road/close/night presets not yet independently reviewed (overview and building both confirmed good).
Select/inspect picking is radius/nearest-based rather than a true mesh raycast — a documented, deliberate simplification given the public API contract, not a bug.
Undo/redo of road/building/animal add-remove changes the entity's id (roads.addRoad/buildings.place/animals.spawn all mint fresh ids) — documented, low-impact.

tools.good: This is the module that makes the game playable rather than watchable, and it delivers: a real tool framework (activate/deactivate/undo/redo >=50 steps), and I independently verified two presets. `overview` shows the full scripted session actually working end-to-end — a curving gravel road crossing the river with a real bridge, a large painted habitat overlay, structures placed — all through the module's own public API, no shortcuts. `building` shows a working ghost preview: the real placed lodge with a semi-transparent red overlay correctly signalling an invalid (occupied) placement. Also found and fixed a genuine bug during its own testing: an unbounded terrain-raise stroke that, under this session's heavy concurrent load, once grew tall enough to embed the camera inside solid terrain — now capped, which fixes real gameplay too. README is thorough: full API, undo/redo mechanics explained per-tool, cost model, and an honest known-gaps list.

issues.text: SYSTEMIC: everything renders washed out toward white — terrain, roads, animal hide, tree bark and foliage all show it. Builders are authoring albedo at roughly the target value, but ACES tone mapping then lifts and desaturates it further. The project-wide fix is to author darker and more saturated than the intended result. This is the single largest thing standing between the current look and the reference photography.
Nothing is placed in the full game: no roads, buildings, habitats or animals appear at start because the park demo module (wave 3) does not exist yet.
Wave 2 still missing zoning, buildings, traffic and tools; wave 3 missing savannah and park. Without tools the game cannot actually be played, only watched.
